events.excerpt: ESMA's third Sanctions Report highlights the need for greater convergence in enforcement 15 October 2026 Market Abuse Supervisory convergence Transparency The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU's financial markets regulator and supervisor, published today its consolidated report on sanctions and measures imposed across the European Economic Area (EEA) in 2025, enhancing the transparency of sanctions data reported under EU financial acts within its remit. In 2025, national authorities across the EEA imposed more than 950 administrative sanctions and measures, a stable number compared with the past two years. The aggregated value of administrative fines amounted to almost €82 million. The report also highlights an increased use of settlements. As in previous years, activity remained focused mainly on breaches of the Market Abuse Regulation and the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive and Regulation. Enforcement activity remained concentrated in a small number of jurisdictions, with Germany, France and Spain accounting for two thirds of the total value of administrative fines across the EEA. events.excerpt: ESMA proposes simpler EU Taxonomy reporting 29 October 2026 Issuer disclosure Sustainable finance The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has published its Final Report providing technical advice to the European Commission on simplifying key performance indicators under the Taxonomy Disclosures Delegated Act. ESMA recommends narrowing the mandatory operating expenditure (OpEx) KPI to non-capitalised research and development expenditure. It also proposes simpler group Taxonomy reporting, including removing the weighted-average KPI, and targeted measures to make disclosures more proportionate, clearer and easier to use. The Technical Advice was coordinated with the other European Supervisory Authorities, in particular on the voluntary use of counterparties’ OpEx information and group-level Taxonomy reporting. The proposals support ESMA’s simplification and burden reduction objectives, while focussing reporting on information that is useful for decision-making, and preserving the relevance, comparability and reliability of Taxonomy disclosures. Next steps ESMA has submitted the Final Report and its technical advice to the European Commission for consideration in its review of the Taxonomy Disclosures Delegated Act. F
events.headline: ESMA proposes simpler EU Taxonomy reporting

events.excerpt: ESMA publishes latest edition of its newsletter 29 October 2026 ESMA newsletter The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has published today the latest edition of its Spotlight on Markets newsletter , covering key activities and publications from September and October 2026. This edition opens with the appointment of Carlo Comporti as ESMA’s next Chair . His appointment was confirmed by the Council of the European Union, and he will take up his position on 1 November 2026. Top news highlights include ESMA’s 2027 Annual Work Programme , setting out priorities for stronger, simpler and more integrated EU capital markets; the new Union Strategic Supervisory Priority on digital innovation; and the European Supervisory Authorities’ priorities for 2027 . Other key publications featured in this edition include: the preparations for the transition to T+1 settlement , the ESAs’ call for vigilance over external dependencies, cyber threats and private markets , ESMA’s proposals to make MiCA clearer, safer and ready for emerging services , and its second Trends, Risks and Vulnerabilities Report of 2026 . events.excerpt: EU seeks nominations for stakeholder group on tokenisation standards in finance 09 November 2026 Digital Finance and Innovation The European Central Bank (ECB), together with the European Commission and the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), is calling upon wholesale financial industry stakeholders to express their interest in joining the European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG). The group will bring together industry stakeholders to develop common standards for an interconnected tokenised financial ecosystem. The group aims to establish a framework for monitoring compliance with the agreed standards and may formulate recommendations for EU authorities on how to incentivise compliance with those standards. Its work will be market-driven and shaped by the contributions and consensus of industry stakeholders. To this end, the ETSG will be chaired by participants from the industry, with the ECB, the Commission and ESMA acting as observers. Participation in the ETSG is open to a wide range of stakeholders, including EU associations, private entities, global institutions, fintech companies and technical providers working on tokenisation or DLT-based financial services, in accordance with its mandate . events.excerpt: ESMA finalises the review of guidelines on the delay in disclosure of inside information 16 October 2026 Guidelines and Technical standards Market Abuse Market Integrity Simplification and Burden Reduction The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has updated and streamlined its Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) guidelines on the delay in the disclosure of inside information , completing the revised regulatory framework. Under MAR, issuers are required to disclose as soon as possible the inside information concerning them, to ensure that investors are informed and to prevent insider dealing. In specific circumstances, issuers may delay public disclosure to avoid prejudicing their legitimate interests. These guidelines help issuers in their decision to delay disclosure by providing a non-exhaustive list of legitimate interests that could justify such delay. events.excerpt: One year to go for T+1 settlement: the regulatory framework is complete, now let’s make it happen 16 October 2026 Guidelines and Technical standards Post Trading Press Releases The European Union (EU) will switch to T+1 settlement on 11 October 2027. Ahead of the transition, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, calls on market participants to finalise technical preparations, assess readiness across their entire ecosystems and begin testing as soon as possible throughout the trading and settlement chain. With the publication of the RTS and ESMA Guidelines on standardised procedures and messaging protocols , the regulatory framework is now ready. The first deadline is for investment firms and their clients to comply with the new requirements on allocations and confirmations from 7 December 2026. Verena Ross, ESMA’s chair, said: “The transition to T+1 is one of the most impactful recent market structure initiatives. It will fundamentally improve the efficiency and international competitiveness of the EU markets. events.headline: One year to go for T+1 settlement: the regulatory framework is complete, now let’s make it happen

events.excerpt: ESMA streamlines several Q&As as part of simplification efforts 22 October 2026 Market Abuse MiFID - Secondary Markets Short Selling Simplification and Burden Reduction The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU regulator and supervisor, has updated its Questions and Answers (Q&As) on market structure under MiFID II , the Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) and the Short Selling Regulation (SSR) , removing outdated, duplicative and no longer relevant guidance as part of its Simplification and Burden Reduction (SBR) initiative . The exercise focused on identifying Q&As that are no longer relevant due to legislative amendments that are reflected in established market practices, or that are covered by other ESMA guidance. As a result, several Q&As have been withdrawn or amended, including instances where the same issues are addressed in other ESMA publications such as supervisory briefings and opinions. The goal of the initiative is to reduce unnecessary complexity, remove obsolete guidance and ensure that ESMA's Q&As remain relevant, proportionate and consistent with the current legislative framework. Stakeholders are encouraged to refer to the updated set of Q&As together with any other ESMA guidance for the most comprehensive interpretation of the applicable rules. Fu
events.headline: ESMA streamlines several Q&As as part of simplification efforts
